topics.label: Introduction to cancer hallmarks and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the learning objectives and frames the discussion around tumor progression models and cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Growth signal autonomy and pathway deregulation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how oncogenic mutations in cell-surface receptors and downstream cascades allow cancer cells to sustain proliferation independently of external growth signals.

topics.label: Blocks to terminal differentiation in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how impaired cellular differentiation contributes to malignancy across hematopoietic and epithelial tissues.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how cancer cells avoid programmed cell death by disrupting the balance of pro- and anti-apoptotic regulators downstream of p53.

topics.label: Replicative immortality and bypass of senescence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the mechanisms of telomere shortening, normal senescence barriers, and how tumors overcome proliferative limits through telomerase activation.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming and oncometabolites in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how tumor cells rewire their metabolic pathways, shift toward aerobic glycolysis, and generate oncometabolites to sustain growth.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the angiogenic switch required to establish new blood vessels for supplying oxygen and nutrients to growing tumors.

topics.label: Mechanisms, detection, and biology of metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the physiological steps, clinical monitoring methods, selective pressures, and genomic features associated with cancer dissemination.

topics.label: Lecture summary and conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer summarizes the key concepts of the lecture and provides closing remarks.
